evals.prompt: I just merged a fix titled 'Fix durable idempotent append replay' on a Rust distributed agent runtime (AgentDB) at /Users/lishen/work/agentdb-dst-verify. The fix touches the append + replay paths. Design a stability test plan for this change. Save it to docs/testing-plans/durable-idempotent-append-replay.md in that repo. Use the project's own runbooks and tooling where possible.
evals.expected_output: A plan file at the named path covering at minimum: append idempotency under client retry storm, replay equivalence after crash mid-append, duplicate suppression under asymmetric partition, durability after simulated fsync loss, concurrent forks observing the same append. Plan must cite catalog references and the project's own docs/runbooks/fault_injected.md and tools/agentdb-cluster-smoke.

evals.prompt: I have a small Raft-based key-value store written in Go (~3k lines, no replication beyond the Raft library itself). I'm about to ship a new feature that lets clients change a key's TTL with the same idempotency guarantee the existing PUT has. Design a focused test plan for this feature. I do not have Jepsen integration yet — propose what to use without assuming Jepsen.
evals.expected_output: A plan that uses property-based testing for the TTL semantics, deterministic-simulation-style scheduling (or a clear acknowledgement that DST requires plumbing the library doesn't have yet), crash-recovery scenarios across the new IO boundary, and a note that linearizability checking with Elle/Porcupine over op histories would be the natural follow-up if/when Jepsen integration exists. Should NOT propose 'just run Jepsen' as if the user can.

evals.prompt: Quick design check — I'm changing a typo in a log line and removing two unused imports in a stateless HTTP handler. What's the right test plan?
evals.expected_output: Early-exit. The skill should explicitly say 'this change does not warrant a distributed test plan' and recommend the lightest appropriate testing (e.g. existing unit tests, lint). Should NOT produce a ceremonial multi-scenario plan.

evals.prompt: Design a release-validation plan for a PostgreSQL-compatible SQL engine. Only single-node builds are available. It has integer, decimal and text columns, constraints, transactions, scans and joins. Current tests exercise integer primary-key reads and writes. We can run a reference PostgreSQL instance. Focus on safety before benchmarking; there is no existing plan.
evals.expected_output: Plan single-client semantic controls and differential generation before concurrent no-fault histories and targeted storage faults. Select SQL semantic coverage across types, mutation paths, scans/aggregates/joins, transaction lifecycle, and drivers/prepare thresholds. Declare multiset/ordering/type/error equivalence, bounded shrinking and narrow reviewed exclusions. Include transaction-local checking without assuming arbitrary concurrent schedules can be compared to a sequential reference. Do not claim replication coverage; no-fault campaigns retain model/history/checker and meaningful budget tiers.

evals.prompt: Review this proposed durability/isolation plan for a database: docs call the default fast mode safe, CLI help says unsafe, and SET SERIALIZABLE returns success. All release binaries print the same version string. The plan runs kill -9, then checks health and a checksum-warning log. Tests currently generate only WAL files, although production flushes table files. What needs to change?
evals.expected_output: Preserve contradictory versioned claims; pin artifact digest, requested/effective settings, driver/checker identity and behavioral probes rather than trusting labels or SET success. Separate process death, unsynced-write loss, IO errors and silent corruption. Require actual table-file/flush coverage and client-visible recovery checks against acknowledged state or documented refusal/repair behavior. Health/checksum logging alone cannot establish safety. Flag untested paths rather than infer coverage.
